summary: Tested the CSRF header guard and the handling of unreadable ZIP members, then ran a full browser regression on the preview URL. Backend: the new file test_csrf_zip_iter16.py passes 16/16. Calls without the header get 403 'Richiesta non consentita', or 403 when the header value is wrong. This was checked on login, logout, refresh, upload, delete invoice, company POST/PATCH/DELETE, users POST/PATCH/password/DELETE, forgot-password and reset-password, and in each case no DB side effect happens. The same calls with the header return 200. GET requests without the header return 200. The CORS preflight is not blocked. The ZIP tests cover a corrupt-CRC member, an encrypted member, an unsupported compression method (99) and a truncated deflate stream. Each case returns HTTP 200 with a per-file result 'File dell'archivio illeggibile, corrotto o protetto da password', and the valid sibling member is imported. zip_lying_size_repro.py no longer raises. Iter15 limits re-verified (sequential run): 51 files -> 400, 50 files OK, 3-level nesting OK / 4-level rejected, 25MB member rejected, >300MB total, >5000 members, DTD/ENTITY rejected, UTF-16 billion laughs, CSV apostrophe prefix, samples import. Full suite with -n0: 110 passed, 8 failed. All 8 failures are stale old tests: they expect an explicit CORS origin while .env has CORS_ORIGINS="*", they omit X-Company-Vat, or they read anagrafiche as a list although it is now paginated. Under the default xdist config (-n --dist loadscope) more old tests fail because they share VAT 01234567890 across workers; this is test isolation, not an app bug. Frontend: on the preview URL every step passed and no 403 appeared. Steps checked: login; create 2 companies, rename, delete (blocked delete with invoices shows a toast); upload of files and of a folder; upload of a corrupt ZIP showing the per-file error plus the imported good member; list; CSV export download; detail page; XML download; delete an invoice (count 4->3); create a user with a P.IVA; add a second P.IVA (shows '2 P.IVA', checked in DB); set the password (bcrypt $2b$ checked in DB); forgot-password form (non-registered TEST email) shows the success message; reset-password with a token seeded in the DB, then login with the new password; reused token -> error; logout; protected route -> /login; delete the user. New finding (parser): a ZIP whose central directory declares a small file_size still gets fully decompressed into memory before the check fails. A 400KB zip produced an 870MB peak in extract_xml_files.

minor.issue: Zip-bomb bypass through a fake file_size. The MAX_MEMBER_BYTES and MAX_ZIP_TOTAL_BYTES checks use info.file_size, which comes from the attacker-controlled central directory. zf.read() on CPython 3.11 calls decompressor.decompress(data, MAX_N≈2GB) and only truncates to file_size afterwards. So a member that declares 1000 bytes is still decompressed to its full size in RAM, and only then does the BadZipFile/CRC error get caught. Measured: a 407KB zip holding a 400MB member that declares 1000 bytes -> 870MB tracemalloc peak in extract_xml_files. A 100MB upload could ask for several GB and OOM the backend. The result is correct (per-file error, no 500); only memory is unbounded. Fix: stream through zf.open(info) in 64KB chunks and abort once the bytes read go over min(MAX_MEMBER_BYTES, remaining budget).

CORS_ORIGINS="*", so allow_credentials=False and ACAO is '*'. This works because the frontend is same-origin, but old tests (test_soft_merge_dedup::test_login_cookies/test_cors_preflight, test_users_auth::test_cors_credentials) expect the explicit origin. Either set an explicit origin list or delete or update those tests.

action_items: Bound decompression in fattura_parser._read_member: read zf.open(info) in chunks and stop after MAX_MEMBER_BYTES (and the remaining _Budget). Do not trust info.file_size.
Optional: clean up stale old tests (CORS explicit origin, missing X-Company-Vat, anagrafiche now paginated) or make them xdist-safe (shared VAT 01234567890 across workers).
critical_code_review_comments: csrf_guard is fine. It is registered before CORSMiddleware, so CORS wraps the 403. OPTIONS is not blocked. The header comparison is exact/case-sensitive on the value, which matches axios.
server.py is 778 lines (>700). Consider splitting the auth, users, companies and invoices routers.
_read_member swallows every read error into one message. That is fine for the user, but nothing is logged, so corrupt uploads are invisible to ops.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/conftest.py (new: adds X-Requested-With to every requests.Session so old tests keep working)

success_rate.backend: 100% of new/targeted tests (16/16 + iter15 security suite); 110/118 overall, 8 stale old tests

seed_data_creation: Temporary TEST companies, users, invoices and a reset token were created. All of them were removed at the end: the DB now holds only the admin user. The admin password is unchanged, and forgot-password was never triggered for the admin.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with -n0 (pytest.ini enables xdist loadscope and old files share VAT 01234567890). conftest.py injects X-Requested-With into all requests Sessions. To test without the header, pop it from the session (see noxrw() in test_csrf_zip_iter16.py). The zip-bomb memory issue can be reproduced at parser level: write a 400MB deflate member, patch the central-dir uncompressed size (offset 24 after PK\x01\x02) to 1000, then measure tracemalloc around extract_xml_files.
rca of the issue: Zip memory: zipfile.ZipExtFile._read1 calls decompress(data, max(n, MIN_READ_SIZE)) with n=MAX_N when read() is called with no size, then slices to _left=file_size. The size guard in extract_xml_files relies on the declared file_size, so the real decompressed size is unbounded until EOF.
